biography: Cassio Cortes, born in the vibrant heart of São Paulo, Brazil, didn't just find racing; racing found him. Growing up amidst the roar of engines from the local go-kart track, young Cassio was captivated. His first taste of competition came at age 12, using a kart cobbled together from spare parts. While his family struggled to afford upgrades, Cassio's raw talent was undeniable. He quickly dominated local karting circuits, earning him a spot in the Copa Fusca series. It was there, behind the wheel of a humble Volkswagen Beetle, that Cassio truly honed his skills. His flamboyant style and fearless overtaking maneuvers quickly made him a fan favorite, and eventually led to his team, Cassio Cortes, where he currently drives. Cassio is now at his peak, aiming for international recognition.
drivingStyle: Cassio's driving is a blend of Brazilian flair and calculated aggression. He's known for his late-braking overtakes and willingness to push the car to its absolute limit. While this can lead to spectacular passes, it also means he occasionally struggles with tire management, often sacrificing long-term pace for short bursts of speed. He thrives under pressure, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest. Cassio is a master of reading track conditions, adapting his driving style on the fly to maximize grip and minimize wear.

rivalries.name: Ricardo Vargas
rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from their early karting days, fueled by constant on-track battles and off-track trash talk.

rivalries.name: Isabela Oliveira
rivalries.reason: A fierce competitor known for her unwavering consistency, representing a direct contrast to Cassio's more impulsive style, leading to tactical clashes.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: A more recent rivalry ignited by a controversial collision during a crucial championship race, with accusations of intentional blocking flying between the two camps.

quirks: Always wears a specific pair of lucky socks, hand-knitted by his grandmother.
Listens to a specific Brazilian Samba song before every race to get pumped up.
Visually inspects each of his tires before getting into the car, regardless of what his engineers say.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about going fast; it's about feeling the rhythm of the road and dancing with the car."
careerHighlight: Winning the Copa Fusca Championship in 2020 after a thrilling final race where he overtook three cars in the last lap, cementing his status as a rising star.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2021 Interlagos Grand Prix, costing him a potential victory and severely damaging his team's morale.
